newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Markets help National Mutual half year results.
newsitem.headline: Markets help National Mutual half year results.

text.p: Life insurer National Mutual Holdings Ltd (NMH) on Tuesday reported a better than expected half-year profit, bolstered by strong investment returns.
"We are delighted with the profit result of A$175 million (US$125 million). We think it's a good half-year result," managing director Geoff Tomlinson told a news conference.
NMH's net earnings surged 18 percent to A$175.52 million for the six months to March 31, about A$40 million higher than analysts' average forecasts of A$134 million.
"It was a big number and mainly driven by investment markets," said Tony Jackson, insurance analyst for Macquarie Equities Ltd.
The group, which listed is shares on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges in October last year, restated its 1996 half year earnings at A$148.3 million from A$131.5 million.
NMH said shareholders had received 6.4 percent growth in value during the half-year, from a four cent per share dividend and a seven cent per share growth in assets.
Australia and New Zealand financial services group National Mutual Life (NML) contributed A$111 million to the result.
NMH's 69 percent owned Hong Kong-based life insurer, National Mutual Asia, which reported its interim results last week, contributed A$67 million.
National Mutual Funds Management (NMFM) contributed A$5 million and Australian Casualty and Life A$6 million, while National Mutual Health Insurance made a A$10 million loss.
Jackson said at the operating level, the result was better than he had anticipated for the group's life business and for National Mutual Asia.

"The result for National Mutual Asia in Hong Kong dollars was exactly as I expected but the Australian profits for that business were substantially higher -- mainly on the investment income side because of a property revaluation," Jackson said.
Jackson said the profit impact of the Hong Kong property revaluation is smoothed over five years for National Mutual Asia, but is taken immediately by its parent.
"The implication of this is there will be investment income rolling off in the Hong Kong (accounts) in the future that has already been accounted for in Australia," he said.
Analysts said a disappointing aspect of the result was the group's failure to make inroads into its capitalised losses.
The company reported a net write-back of capitalised losses of A$12 million in the half-year, due to better information available to assess those losses, but NML continued to face problems on costs.
"The risk products area is one area that's really hurting us at the present time and we are finding stiff competition," NML managing director Tony Killen told the news conference.
Capitalised losses now amount to about A$100 million.
Killen said he was confident these could be written back over the next two years with further attacks on costs.
"Provided they can get the sales coming back there (risk products) then you should start to see some further per unit expense reductions," a Sydney-based analyst said.
The company's stock closed steady at A$1.95 on turnover of 4.5 million shares. National Mutual valued its own shares at A$1.80 each, up from A$1.73 at its September 31 balance date.
